p.src: The Great Way is profound and hidden; how can its secret be known? Once revealed, it startles ghosts and gods. It enfolds the universe and cleaves open the mystic light; no worldly joy can compare with true bliss. Before Vulture Peak, the precious pearl is held aloft, shining brightly with fivefold radiance. It illumines all beings above and below throughout heaven and earth; those who comprehend it live as long as mountains and seas.

p.src: Now Tripitaka and his three disciples took leave of the woodcutter, descended Hidden Mist Mountain, and set out along the main road. After traveling for several days, they suddenly saw a walled city close ahead. Tripitaka said, “Wukong, look at that city ahead. Could it be the land of India?” The Pilgrim waved his hand and said, “No, no. Although the Tathagata’s abode is called the Land of Supreme Bliss, there is no walled city there. It is a great mountain, with towers and halls among its peaks, called Thunderclap Monastery on Vulture Peak. Even when we reach India, we shall not yet be at the Tathagata’s abode. Who knows how far India still lies from Vulture Peak? That city is probably an outlying prefecture of India. We shall know for certain when we reach it.”

p.src: Before long they reached the city outskirts. Tripitaka dismounted and passed through three successive gates, where he found the people’s affairs desolate and the streets deserted. When they came to the marketplace, they saw many men in blue arrayed on either side, while several officials in caps and sashes stood beneath the eaves. The four travelers proceeded down the street, but none of those people yielded or stepped aside. Zhu Bajie, boorish and simple, thrust out his long snout and cried, “Make way! Make way!” They jerked up their heads, and at the sight of him their bones went weak and their sinews numb. Stumbling and staggering, they all cried, “A monster has come! A monster has come!” The capped officials beneath the eaves were so frightened that they trembled all over. Bowing, they asked, “Where have you come from?” Fearing that his disciples might cause trouble, Tripitaka stepped firmly to the front and addressed the crowd: “This poor monk comes from the Great Tang in the Eastern Land, sent by imperial command to worship the Buddha at Thunderclap Monastery in India and seek the scriptures. Passing through your honored region, we neither know its name nor have yet found lodging. Having only just entered the city, we failed to step respectfully aside. p.src: After reading it, the Pilgrim asked the officials, “What does ‘Prefect Shangguan’ mean?” The officials replied, “Shangguan is a surname. It is the surname of our prefect.” The Pilgrim laughed and said, “That is a rare surname.” Bajie said, “Brother, you have never studied books. Near the end of the Hundred Family Surnames there is a line, ‘Shangguan, Ouyang.’” Tripitaka said, “Disciples, enough idle talk. If any of you can pray for rain, bring them a shower of blessed rain to relieve the people’s suffering. That would be a deed of immeasurable goodness. If none of you can, then let us move on and not delay our journey.” The Pilgrim said, “What is so difficult about praying for rain? Overturning rivers and stirring seas, shifting the Dipper and moving the stars, kicking heaven and troubling the wells, breathing mist and spouting clouds, bearing mountains and driving the moon, summoning rain and calling the wind—which of these was not a mere childhood game for old Monkey? What is remarkable about it?”

p.src: On hearing this, the officials ordered two of their number to hurry to the prefectural office and report, “My lord, an immeasurably joyous event has come upon us!” The prefect was burning incense and praying silently. Delighted to hear the report of good news, he immediately asked, “What good news?” The official replied, “Today, just as we carried the proclamation to the marketplace and were about to hang it up, four monks appeared. They said they had been sent from the Great Tang in the Eastern Land to worship the Buddha and seek scriptures at Great Thunderclap Monastery in India. The moment they saw the proclamation, they said they could pray down blessed rain, so we came especially to inform you.”

p.src: The prefect immediately straightened his robes and set out on foot. Taking neither sedan chair nor horse nor a large retinue, he went directly to the marketplace to invite them with due ceremony. Suddenly someone announced, “His lordship the prefect has arrived!” The crowd moved aside. At the sight of the Tang Monk, the prefect showed no fear of his hideous disciples, but prostrated himself in the middle of the street and said, “I am Shangguan, prefect of Fengxian Prefecture. Having purified myself with incense and ablutions, I humbly beg you, reverend master, to pray for rain and save the people. I pray that you will show great compassion, wield your divine powers, and deliver us from our plight.” Tripitaka returned his courtesy and said, “This is no place for discussion. Once this poor monk reaches a monastery or temple, we can properly set about the matter.” The prefect said, “Reverend master, please come with us to my humble office. There is a clean and quiet place there.”

p.src: Hearing this, the Pilgrim’s face lit up with joy, and he laughed aloud. “Say no more, say no more! If you speak of a thousand pieces of gold as reward, you will not get so much as half a drop of blessed rain. But if we speak only of accumulating merit and virtue, old Monkey will send you a mighty rainstorm.” The prefect was in fact an upright and worthy man with a deep love for his people. He immediately invited the Pilgrim to take the honored seat, then bowed low and said, “If the reverend master truly shows us compassion, I shall certainly never act contrary to virtue.” The Pilgrim said, “No more talk for now. Please rise. I ask only that you take good care of my master while old Monkey attends to the matter.” Sha Monk asked, “Brother, how will you go about it?” The Pilgrim replied, “You and Bajie come over here and stand below this hall to lend me support while old Monkey summons a dragon to make rain.” Bajie and Sha Monk obediently followed his instructions, and all three stood below the hall. The prefect burned incense and bowed in worship. Tripitaka sat reciting scriptures.

p.src: The Pilgrim recited the True Words and chanted an incantation. At once a black cloud appeared in the east and gradually descended before the hall. It was Ao Guang, the old Dragon King of the Eastern Sea. Ao Guang drew in the skirts of his cloud, transformed into human form, and came forward. Bowing to the Pilgrim, he said, “Great Sage, you summoned this little dragon. Where do you wish to employ me?” The Pilgrim said, “Please rise. I have troubled you to come from afar, though it is no great matter. This is Fengxian Prefecture, which has suffered drought for years. Why have you not come to send rain?” The old dragon replied, “May the Great Sage be informed: although I can make rain, I am one who acts only when dispatched by Heaven. If Heaven does not send me, how would I dare come here and make rain on my own authority?” The Pilgrim said, “Passing through this region, I saw that the people suffer from the long drought, so I specially summoned you to bestow rain and bring them relief. Why do you make excuses?” The Dragon King said, “How would I dare make excuses? When the Great Sage recited the True Words and summoned me, I dared not fail to come. First, I have received no imperial decree from Heaven; second, I have not brought the divine generals who administer rain. How, then, could I set the Rain Department in motion? Since the Great Sage is resolved to bring relief, permit this little dragon to return to the sea and muster my forces. Meanwhile, please go to the Celestial Palace and obtain approval, requesting a sacred decree for rain, and ask the water officials to release the dragons. Then I shall be able to send rain in the measure specified by the decree.”

p.src: When the pilgrim heard him explain the reason, he had no choice but to release the old Dragon King and send him back to the sea. He then leapt out of the magic circle and told the Tang Monk the whole affair of the Dragon King. The Tang Monk said, “Since that is so, go and see to it, but by no means make an empty promise.” The pilgrim immediately instructed Bajie and Sha Monk, “Protect Master while I go up to the Celestial Palace.” What a Great Sage! No sooner had he said he was leaving than he silently vanished. The prefect, trembling with fear, asked, “Where has Lord Sun gone?” Bajie laughed and said, “He has ridden a cloud up to Heaven.” The prefect became exceedingly reverent and sent out urgent proclamations ordering every household throughout the city, in every avenue and alley, whether belonging to nobles or commoners, soldiers or civilians, to enshrine a tablet to the Dragon Kings, place a jar of pure water at the door with willow sprigs in it, tend incense offerings, and worship Heaven. Of this no more need be said.

p.src: Now the pilgrim mounted his Somersault Cloud and went straight to the Western Gate of Heaven. There he saw the Heaven-supporting King who Guards the Realm leading celestial soldiers and mighty warriors forward to welcome him, saying, “Great Sage, have you completed the task of obtaining the scriptures?” The pilgrim replied, “It is not far from completion. We have now reached the borders of the Kingdom of India, where there is an outlying prefecture called Phoenix-Immortal Prefecture. No rain has fallen there for three years, and the people are suffering greatly, so I wish to pray for rain and save them. I summoned the Dragon King there, but he said that without an edict he dared not bring rain on his own authority. I have therefore come especially to request an edict from the Jade Emperor.” The Heavenly King said, “I suspect rain is not meant to fall in that place. Some time ago I heard that the prefect behaved outrageously and offended Heaven and Earth. The Lord on High found him guilty and set up a mountain of rice, a mountain of flour, and a great golden lock; rain is not to fall until all three have been worn away.” The pilgrim did not understand what this meant and wished to see the Jade Emperor. The Heavenly King dared not obstruct him and let him pass. He went straight to the outside of the Hall of Perfect Light, where the Four Great Celestial Masters came forward to greet him, asking, “What brings the Great Sage here?” The pilgrim replied, “While escorting the Tang Monk, I reached Phoenix-Immortal Prefecture on the borders of India. As no rain has fallen there, the prefect invited my master to pray for rain. I summoned the Dragon King, intending to order him to bring rain, but he said that without an edict from the Jade Emperor he dared not act on his own. So I have come especially to request an edict and relieve the people’s distress.” The Four Great Celestial Masters said, “Rain is not meant to fall in that region.” The pilgrim laughed and said, “Whether it should or should not, I must trouble you to present my request and see how much weight my influence carries.” Immortal Elder Ge said, “As the common saying goes: ‘A fly wraps itself in a web—what an enormous face!’” Xu Jingyang said, “Enough idle talk. Let us simply take him inside.”

p.src: Qiu Hongji, Zhang Daoling, Ge, and Xu, the four Perfected Immortals, led him beneath the Hall of Miraculous Mist and reported, “Your Majesty, Sun Wukong has reached Phoenix-Immortal Prefecture in the Kingdom of India on his journey and wishes to obtain rain for it. He has come especially to request an edict.” The Jade Emperor said, “On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month three years ago, We went forth to inspect the myriad heavens and journey through the Three Realms. When Our carriage reached that place, We saw that the impious official had overturned the vegetarian offerings prepared for Heaven and fed them to the dogs, all while uttering filthy abuse. For this offense against Heaven, We immediately established three things within the Hall of Wafting Fragrance. Take Sun Wukong to see them. If all three have been worn away, We shall issue an edict for him; but if they have not, tell him to cease meddling in affairs that do not concern him.”

p.src: The Four Celestial Masters led the pilgrim into the Hall of Wafting Fragrance to look. There stood a mountain of rice some hundred feet high, and a mountain of flour some two hundred feet high. Beside the rice mountain was a chicken no bigger than a fist, pecking at the rice with one quick peck and then one slow peck. Beside the flour mountain was a golden-haired Pekingese, licking up the flour with one long stroke of its tongue and then one short stroke. On the left stood an iron frame from which hung a golden lock some thirteen or fourteen inches long, its bolt as thick as a finger. Beneath it was a bright lamp whose flame licked at the bolt. Not understanding their meaning, the pilgrim turned and asked the Celestial Masters, “What does all this mean?” A Celestial Master replied, “That fellow offended Heaven, so the Jade Emperor established these three things. Only when the chicken has pecked up all the rice, the dog has licked up all the flour, and the lamp flame has burned through the lock bolt will rain be permitted to fall in that region.”

p.src: On hearing this, the pilgrim turned pale with astonishment. He dared make no further petition, but walked out of the hall with shame written all over his face. The Four Celestial Masters laughed and said, “Great Sage, you need not be troubled. This matter can be resolved only through the practice of goodness. If but one compassionate and virtuous thought should move Heaven, the mountains of rice and flour would collapse at once, and the lock bolt would immediately break. Go and persuade him to return to goodness, and blessings will come of themselves.” The pilgrim followed their advice. Without returning to the Hall of Miraculous Mist to take leave of the Jade Emperor, he went straight down to the mortal world. In a short while he reached the Western Gate of Heaven and again saw the Heaven-supporting King who Guards the Realm. The Heavenly King asked, “How did your request for an edict fare?” The pilgrim recounted the whole business of the rice mountain, the flour mountain, and the golden lock, then said, “It was just as you said: the Jade Emperor would not issue an edict. Just now, when the Celestial Masters saw me out, they told me to persuade that fellow to return to goodness, and then blessings would spring from their true source.” He then took his leave, lowered his cloud, and descended to the mortal world.

p.src: The prefect, together with Tripitaka, Bajie, Wujing, and officials high and low, came crowding around to meet him and ply him with questions. Monkey gave the prefect a sharp rebuke: “Because you, wretch that you are, offended Heaven and Earth on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month three years ago, the common people have been made to suffer, and even now no rain will fall.” The terrified prefect prostrated himself and said, “Master, how did you learn of what happened three years ago?” Monkey said, “Why did you overturn the vegetarian offerings prepared for the sacrifice to Heaven and feed them to the dogs? Tell me the whole truth.” The prefect dared conceal nothing. “On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month three years ago,” he said, “I presented offerings and held a sacrifice to Heaven here in my own residence. My ill-tempered wife quarreled with me using bitter words, and in a moment of ignorant rage I overturned the offering table and spilled the vegetarian dishes. It is true that I called the dogs to eat them. For the past two years the memory has weighed on my mind, leaving my thoughts dazed and troubled, with nowhere to seek absolution. I did not know that Heaven had found me guilty and brought calamity upon the people. Now that you have graciously come, Master, I earnestly beg you to reveal what judgment the celestial realm has passed.” Monkey said, “That very day was when the Jade Emperor descended to the mortal world. He saw you feed the sacrificial offerings to the dogs and heard the filthy words from your mouth, so he immediately established three conditions against you.” Bajie asked, “What three conditions are those?” Monkey replied, “In the Hall of Fragrant Offerings stands a mountain of rice about a hundred feet high; and a mountain of flour about two hundred feet high. Beside the rice mountain is a chick no bigger than a fist, pecking at the rice, now quickly and now slowly; beside the flour mountain is a golden-haired lapdog, licking at the flour with strokes of its tongue, now long and now short. To the left stands an iron frame, from which hangs a great golden lock with a shackle as thick as a finger. Below it burns a bright lamp, whose flame licks at the lock’s shackle. Only when the chick has pecked up all the rice, the dog has licked up all the flour, and the lamp has burned through the shackle will rain be due to fall here.” Bajie laughed. “That is no great matter, no great matter at all. If Elder Brother will take me there, I shall assume my gigantic magic body, eat all their rice and flour in a single sitting, and break the shackle. Then rain is certain to fall.” Monkey said, “Idiot, stop talking nonsense. Those are devices established by Heaven. How could you even see them?” Tripitaka said, “If that is so, what are we to do?” “It is not difficult, not difficult,” said Monkey. “When I was leaving, the Four Celestial Masters told me that the matter could be resolved simply by doing good.” Prostrate upon the ground, the prefect pleaded piteously, “I shall follow every instruction you give me, Master, and submit to them all.” Monkey said, “If you turn your heart toward goodness, begin without delay to invoke the Buddha’s name and read the scriptures, and I shall still act on your behalf; but if you persist in your former ways and refuse to change, even I cannot absolve you. Before long Heaven will strike you down, and your life will be forfeit.”

p.src: The prefect knocked his head upon the ground in reverence and vowed to mend his ways. He immediately summoned the local Buddhist and Daoist clergy to establish a ritual sanctuary. Each prepared and dispatched memorials to the Three Heavens. Leading the multitude, the prefect offered incense and worshipped, thanking Heaven and Earth while confessing and reproaching himself for his sin. Tripitaka also recited sutras for him. Meanwhile, urgent notices were issued ordering every household, great or small, inside and outside the city, and every man and woman alike, to burn incense and invoke the Buddha’s name. From that moment, pious voices filled every ear. Only then was Monkey delighted. He said to Bajie and Wujing, “Take good care of Master, both of you, while old Monkey makes one more quick journey.” Bajie asked, “Where are you going now, Elder Brother?” Monkey replied, “This prefect has heeded old Monkey’s words and truly accepted instruction. He now reveres goodness and compassion and invokes the Buddha’s name with a sincere heart. I shall go and petition the Jade Emperor once more, and ask him to send some rain.” Wujing said, “Since you mean to go, Elder Brother, do not delay, for this is holding up our journey. You must obtain a good downpour, so that our meritorious purpose may be fulfilled.”

p.src: The great Sage mounted his cloud once more and went straight to the gates of Heaven, where again he met the Heavenly King Protector of the Realm. The Heavenly King asked, “What have you come for this time?” Monkey replied, “The prefect has now turned to goodness.” The Heavenly King too was pleased. While they were speaking, they saw a Writ-Bearing Messenger arrive at the gates of Heaven, holding Daoist memorials and Buddhist dispatches for delivery. When the messenger saw Monkey, he bowed and said, “These good intentions are the fruit of the Great Sage’s work in exhorting the people to virtue.” Monkey asked, “Where are you taking these documents?” The messenger replied, “Straight to the Hall of Luminous Understanding, where I shall hand them to the Celestial Masters to convey before the Great Celestial Worthy, the Jade Emperor.” Monkey said, “In that case, go on ahead. I shall follow behind you.” The messenger passed through the gates of Heaven. The Heavenly King Protector of the Realm said, “Great Sage, there is no need to see the Jade Emperor. Simply go to the Palace of the Primordial Lord Responding to Heaven in the Ninth Firmament and borrow a few thunder gods. Have them go straight there to sound the thunder and flash the lightning, and rain will fall for them.”

p.src: Monkey did indeed follow his advice. Passing through the gates of Heaven, he did not go up to the Hall of Miraculous Mist to request a decree, but turned his cloud steps directly toward the Palace of the Primordial Lord Responding to Heaven in the Ninth Firmament. There the Messenger of the Thunder Gate, the Registrar of Impeachments, and the Inspector Registrar all came to greet him and bowed, saying, “What brings the Great Sage here?” Monkey said, “I have business with the Celestial Worthy.” The three messengers immediately went in to announce him. The Celestial Worthy descended at once from his nine-phoenix throne backed by rosy clouds, straightened his robes, and came out to welcome him. When they had exchanged courtesies, Monkey said, “I have come especially to ask one favor.” The Celestial Worthy asked, “What is it?” Monkey replied, “While escorting the Tang Monk, I reached Fengxian Prefecture and saw how severe the drought was. I have already promised to obtain rain for them, so I have come especially to ask that you lend me some officers and generals from your honored department to go there and sound the thunder.” The Celestial Worthy said, “I know that the prefect offended Heaven and that three conditions were established against him, but I do not know whether rain ought yet to fall.” Monkey laughed and said, “Yesterday I already saw the Jade Emperor and requested a decree. The Jade Emperor ordered the Celestial Masters to lead me to the Hall of Fragrant Offerings to see the three conditions: the mountain of rice, the mountain of flour, and the golden lock. Only when all three have been exhausted or broken will rain be due to fall. I despaired of ever seeing them exhausted, but the Celestial Masters instructed me to persuade the prefect and his people to do good, for when human beings cherish good thoughts, Heaven is sure to heed them. In this way, perhaps Heaven’s heart might be moved and the calamity relieved. Now good thoughts have suddenly arisen, and pious voices fill every ear. A moment ago, the Writ-Bearing Messenger already carried to the Jade Emperor the documents reporting how they have changed their ways and turned to goodness. That is why old Monkey has come especially to your honored palace to ask that you lend me officers and generals of the Thunder Department to assist me.” The Celestial Worthy said, “Since that is so, I shall dispatch Deng, Xin, Zhang, and Tao to lead the Lady of Lightning and descend at once with the Great Sage to Fengxian Prefecture to sound the thunder.”

p.src: Let us leave aside for now how the Great Sage Sun directed the thunder generals to flash lightning and peal thunder over Fengxian Prefecture, causing everyone to turn to goodness. Meanwhile, the heavenly messenger on duty delivered the petitions from the Buddhist and Daoist communities to the Hall of Divine Light, and the Four Celestial Masters conveyed them to the Hall of Miraculous Mist. When the Jade Emperor read them, he said, “Since those people have conceived good intentions, let us see what has become of the three things.” Just as he spoke, an officer guarding the Hall of Fragrant Offerings suddenly reported, “The mountains of rice and flour have both collapsed. In an instant all the rice and flour vanished, and the lock-bar has broken as well.” Before this report was finished, another heavenly officer in attendance brought in the local earth god, city god, gods of the soil, and other deities of Fengxian Prefecture, who all bowed and memorialized: “The prefect and every family among the people of the city, high and low, have without a single exception embraced the fruits of goodness, revering the Buddha and honoring Heaven. We now implore Your Majesty to extend compassion and send down sweet rain everywhere to save the common people.” The Jade Emperor was delighted to hear this and immediately decreed: “Let the Departments of Wind, Cloud, and Rain each obey the command and descend to the mortal world. Within the bounds of Fengxian Prefecture, at this very day and hour, sound the thunder, spread the clouds, and send down three feet and forty-two points of rain.” The Four Great Celestial Masters received the decree and transmitted it to the several departments, which promptly descended to the mortal realm, each displaying its divine might as they all sprang into action together.

p.src: The Great Sage then descended from his cloud and said to Tripitaka, “The matter is settled and the people are safe. We can pack up and be on our way.” When the prefect heard this, he hurriedly bowed and said, “Master Sun, how can you speak so? What you have done for us is a favor of boundless and immeasurable virtue. I have sent men to prepare a modest banquet here, that we may repay your great kindness. I shall also purchase land from the people to build a monastery for you gentlemen, erect shrines in your honor while you yet live, and carve your names upon a stele, so that sacrifices may be offered in all four seasons. Even if we carved your kindness into our bones and engraved it upon our hearts, we could not repay one ten-thousandth of it. How can you already speak of leaving?” Tripitaka said, “Your words are quite proper, sir, but we are wandering monks bound for the Western Heaven, lodging wherever we may. We dare not stay long and shall certainly leave within a day or two.” But the prefect would not hear of letting them go. That very night he sent many men to prepare the feast and begin construction of the shrine.

p.src: One day a feast, the next a banquet; Thanks today, rewards tomorrow. They detained the pilgrims for nearly half a month, waiting only for the monastery and the living shrine to be completed. One day, the prefect invited all four pilgrims to inspect them. The Tang Monk exclaimed in astonishment, “This was a vast undertaking. How was it completed so quickly?” The prefect replied, “I pressed the workmen to labor day and night without rest and ordered them to finish with all haste, especially so that I might invite you gentlemen to inspect it.” Pilgrim laughed and said, “You truly are a worthy, capable, and excellent prefect.” They immediately entered the new monastery. Seeing its lofty halls and pavilions and its splendid mountain gate, they praised it without end. Pilgrim asked his master to bestow a name upon the monastery. Tripitaka said, “Very well. Let the name I leave be ‘Monastery of the Sweet Rain That Brings Universal Deliverance.’” The prefect acclaimed it, saying, “Excellent, excellent!” He issued invitations inscribed in gold to recruit a community of monks to tend the incense offerings. To the left of the main hall, shrines in honor of the four pilgrims while they yet lived were erected, where sacrifices would be offered in each of the four seasons; temples were also built to the Thunder God, the Dragon Gods, and the other deities, in gratitude for their divine aid. When they had finished their inspection, the pilgrims immediately ordered that preparations be hastened for their departure.

p.src: When the people throughout the prefecture realized that the pilgrims could not be persuaded to remain, each prepared farewell gifts, but the pilgrims would not accept so much as a penny. Thus all the prefecture’s officials and people brought out a great array of drums and music and unfurled banners and canopies to escort them for nearly thirty li. Still unable to bear the parting, they watched through tear-filled eyes until the pilgrims disappeared from sight, and only then returned. Indeed, it was just as the saying goes:
